articles.title: Multi-Label Text Classification with Node.js LLMs: Exact JSON for Invoice Field Tagging
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for extracting fields from media supplier invoices, use chat completions with a taxonomy embedded in the request, require a small JSON contract, and reject every label outside that taxon…
articles.body: Short answer: for extracting fields from media supplier invoices, use chat completions with a taxonomy embedded in the request, require a small JSON contract, and reject every label outside that taxonomy. This keeps quality decisions in application code while giving the LLM a bounded text classification task. The same pattern applies to ecommerce product tagging when the product vocabulary is controlled. The operational constraint is quality versus latency. A taxonomy with 18 useful labels is a different system from one with 480 near-duplicates: the latter consumes more input tokens, takes longer to inspect, and creates more ways to disagree with the business rule.

articles.body: Give the agent the script, one visual line per shot, and let it call a local footage index for each line. It comes back with a best clip and two alternatives per line, saves the result as a project you can trim by hand, and exports an MP4 or an FCPXML that opens in Resolve, Premiere or Final Cut with your original files linked. A rough cut is mostly retrieval. For each beat of the script you go looking for a shot that fits, drop it on the timeline, and move on. The judgement is in the last ten percent; the first ninety is searching. That makes it a good job for an agent, as long as the agent has something faster than scrubbing to search with. articles.title: TIL: Why GBase Database Installation May Require Python 2
articles.excerpt: Yesterday, I helped troubleshoot a failed GBase Database(GBase 8a) installation in a POC environment. The error was a Python SyntaxError near the beginning of SetSysEnv.py. The engineer confirmed that…
articles.body: Yesterday, I helped troubleshoot a failed GBase Database(GBase 8a) installation in a POC environment. The error was a Python SyntaxError near the beginning of SetSysEnv.py . The engineer confirmed that Python 2 was installed. But when we checked the default interpreter, we found the real problem: which python python -V The python command pointed to /usr/bin/python3 . Python 2 was installed, but the installation script was running under Python 3. That small difference can prevent a GBase Database installation script from parsing correctly. Reinstalling the package or changing file permissions won't fix an interpreter mismatch. 1. Check the Python Version Before Installing Some GBase Database(GBase 8a) installation packages use Python 2 scripts.

articles.title: Three Times My Test Failed and the LLM Was Right
articles.excerpt: A test fails, and the reflex is: the code is wrong. Debug the code, fix the code, move on. That reflex is usually right, and it's exactly why it took three separate failures to notice it wasn't right…
articles.body: A test fails, and the reflex is: the code is wrong. Debug the code, fix the code, move on. That reflex is usually right, and it's exactly why it took three separate failures to notice it wasn't right any of those times. Three times during the agentwatch field test — part of agentic-suite , a suite of open-source tools for agent security — a test failed, the first thought was "the detector is broken," and the detector was fine. The test was wrong. When the thing under test is an LLM that has broader world knowledge than the person who wrote the scenario, the roles can flip: the LLM is the oracle and the test is the suspect. Case 1: the goal drift that wasn't GoalDriftDetector is supposed to fire when an agent chases a different objective than planned.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.
